documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Six months after zoledronic acid: alkaline phosphatase now in the normal range and thigh pain improved. Will repeat alk phos yearly; retreatment only if it rises or symptoms return.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine. Feels well. Endo says Paget's labs normalized.
Labs today show creatinine 1.8, eGFR now under 45 — restaging CKD to 3b. Potassium fine, urine albumin normal.
Discussed: keep BP controlled, avoid NSAIDs, contrast caution.
Exam: unremarkable.
Plan: continue meds. BMP again in summer. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Emergency department note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — visit 07/05/2025
72M with hypertensive retinopathy and Paget disease. Two hours ago, while reading, a shadow came down over the vision of his right eye. Painless, no improvement since. Several weeks of mild fatigue and general aching, did not seek care. No trauma, no double vision, no discharge.
Vitals: T 37.8 C, P 78, BP 136/72, RR 16.
Exam: tender right temple with diminished temporal pulse. Reports jaw discomfort when chewing.
Labs: ESR 88 mm/h, CRP 74 mg/L.
Impression: giant cell arteritis with right eye vision loss.
Treatment: prednisone 60 mg daily started in the ED. Ophthalmology contacted; temporal artery biopsy scheduled this week. Discharged with close follow-up. PCP to follow sugars on steroids.
Allergies: NKDA.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen Saturday in the ED with sudden right-eye vision loss, temple tenderness, jaw pain, high ESR/CRP — giant cell arteritis. On prednisone 60 mg daily since Saturday. Biopsy Thursday. Ophthalmology following the eye. Headache and jaw better already; fatigue persists. Wife driving him.
Sugars: borrowed his neighbor's meter, fasting readings 160s-180s.
Exam: right temple mildly tender. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P
1. GCA on high-dose prednisone: rheumatology referral to manage taper. Biopsy 7/10.
2. Steroid hyperglycemia: will get him a meter and strips, check fasting and pre-supper. Continue metformin. Call if >300.
3. HTN, CKD: BMP today.

reports.text: Right temporal artery, biopsy, 2.2 cm segment. Transmural granulomatous inflammation centered on the media with multinucleated giant cells and fragmentation of the internal elastic lamina; intimal thickening.

documents.title: Temporal artery biopsy pathology (outside)
documents.author: pathology
documents.body: Outside pathology report received; see result.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation (outside)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Seen 08/05/2025. Biopsy-proven giant cell arteritis with right eye involvement in July. Symptoms resolved on prednisone 60 mg. Reducing to 40 mg daily now, then gradual taper over the coming months per our schedule. Will see every 6-8 weeks. Glucose monitoring by PCP appreciated.

documents.title: Sugar numbers
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Fasting 150s and before supper as high as 240 since the prednisone. Rheumatology lowered me to 40. Is this okay or do I need something?

documents.title: Re: Sugar numbers
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those are what we expect on this much prednisone and they should come down as the dose goes down. Nothing over 300, so no change for now. Keep logging and send me numbers in 3 weeks or sooner if over 300.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: HD flu left deltoid, Pfizer 2025-26 COVID right. On prednisone, aware response may be less. Fine.

documents.title: Emergency department note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED — 11/02/2025
73-year-old man, HTN, DM2, CKD and recent giant cell arteritis, with 12 hours of sudden, severe, sharp upper abdominal pain going through to his back. Had a cardiac catheterization two weeks ago to evaluate chest pain.
Meds listed: aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 5. NKDA.
VS: BP 150/90, HR 98, T 37.2.
Exam: epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding, bowel sounds present, no jaundice, no ascites. Bluish toes; lacy violaceous mottling of the skin of both legs.
Labs: WBC 14.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250. Amylase 800, lipase 900. Creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.8). AST 45, ALT 50, T bili 1.2.
Dx: acute pancreatitis. IV fluids, analgesia, antiemetic. Admitted to medicine.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (20 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 11/2 with acute pancreatitis (lipase 900), admitted three nights per patient; discharge summary not yet received. Back to eating normally before discharge, no pain now. No alcohol ever.
Also learned today: in late October he had a cardiac catheterization through his cardiologist after some chest pain. He says no stent was placed and no medicines were changed. No chest pain since. We don't have that report.
Prednisone: rheumatology has him at 20 mg daily now.
Exam: abdomen soft, nontender. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
A/P
1. Acute pancreatitis, resolved clinically. CMP, CBC, lipase today.
2. Cardiac cath: request report from cardiology.
3. GCA on prednisone 20, per rheumatology. A1c today.
4. CKD 3b: creatinine 2.1 in ED; recheck today.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed request to outside cardiology group for cath report (approx 10/20/25) and last office note, and to hospital for 11/2-11/5 discharge summary. Will follow up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs after the hospital: lipase back to normal, kidney number improving toward your usual, A1c higher from the prednisone as expected. No changes.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's wife called to cancel tomorrow's AWV, he is worn out after a rheumatology appointment and a busy week. Will rebook after the holidays.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up (outside)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Visit 01/13/2026: no headache, jaw pain or new visual symptoms. Inflammatory markers normal. Prednisone reduced to 10 mg daily; continuing slow taper.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (10 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked visit. On prednisone 10 mg now. Sugars lower than in the fall, fasting 120s-140s.
Cardiology report and hospital summary still not received despite request; re-sent.
No abdominal pain since November.
Exam: BP as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet ok.
A1c drawn today; expect it to stay up while on prednisone and drift down after. Continue metformin.
RTC May.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Glucose test strips and lancets, plus amlodipine and lisinopril 90-day, sent.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chronic f/u, wife present. She asked to speak first: over the past several weeks he repeats questions, forgets conversations from the same day, and got muddled doing the household bills, which he has done for 40 years. Some confusion about the day. He thinks she's overstating it but agrees he is "foggy."
No headache, jaw pain or vision change. No falls. Prednisone now 5 mg per rheumatology.
Exam: alert, pleasant, but vague on recent events. Cognitive screen today: missed delayed recall items, clock drawing disorganized. Speech fluent. No focal weakness. Gait normal.
A/P
1. New cognitive decline over weeks, faster than typical. Labs today: CBC, CMP, B12, TSH. Urgent neurology referral. Wife to drive; he agreed to stop driving for now.
2. GCA: prednisone 5 mg, rheumatology managing.
3. DM/HTN/CKD: A1c today. BP a bit above goal today; home readings have been fine, no change.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mrs. Wells, writing to you both as discussed. Blood counts, B12, thyroid and chemistry are normal; kidney number is at his usual. A1c 7.2, better. Nothing in the blood explains the memory change, so the neurology visit is the next step. The referral went out marked urgent.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called: neurology appointment is 7/3, earliest they had. She feels he is a bit worse, more confused in the evenings, but safe at home and eating. No falls, no fever. Advised she can call neurology for cancellation list; ED if sudden change, weakness or fall. PCP aware.

documents.title: Neurology consultation (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY — visit 07/03/2026
73-year-old man with a history of colon cancer and giant cell arteritis, seen with his wife for about three months of quickly worsening memory loss, confusion and sudden jerking movements. She says the decline has accelerated in the past month and he now sometimes does not recognize family members.
Meds per wife: metformin, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Exam: disoriented, has difficulty following commands. Myoclonic jerks of both upper extremities.
Routine blood work normal.
MRI brain: diffuse cortical atrophy; no stroke or mass.
EEG: sharp, triphasic, synchronous discharges.
Impression: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Lumbar puncture for CSF studies being arranged. Discussed with his wife at length.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Lumbar puncture 07/14/2026. CSF RT-QuIC positive, consistent with sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Results reviewed with Mrs. Wells on 08/07. Care is supportive. We discussed palliative care involvement and support at home; she will speak with his primary care physician. Infection control guidance for any future procedures given. Neurology will continue to follow.

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mrs. Wells called after the neurology results. Wants to sit down with PCP about care at home and what help is available. He is home, eating with help, sleeping more. Booked 9/1 at 2:00, 40 minutes. PCP to call her before then.

documents.title: PCP call back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Mrs. Wells. Sorry for this news. Talked through what the visit on 9/1 can cover. She has the neurology letter. She'll bring his pill bottles and the health care proxy form.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: metformin and atorvastatin 90-day. Sent per protocol; PCP to review all meds at 9/1 visit.
